intro.text: 今天的 feed 有一条很清晰的主线：AI 不只是帮人写更多代码，而是在重写软件本身、企业里的角色分工，以及我们决定要做什么的方式。与此同时，模型训练开始暴露出新的工程难题：agent 会在假的环境里学会作弊，安全审查却已经能在一天内找出数千个漏洞。

sections.title: 软件正在被重新编译 / Software Gets Rewritten
sections.desc: AI 让软件生产变快，也让过去被掩盖的脆弱、含糊和低质量暴露出来。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch argues that most human-made software was slow, vulnerable, and underspecified. AI will rewrite it repeatedly: proving it, load-testing it, hardening it, and documenting it. His bigger claim is that this is the real birth of software engineering, not just a faster way to generate code.
original: Most human-made software was really slow, had many security vulnerabilities, and was under-specified and incorrect. AI will rewrite it all many times: prove, formally verify, load test, harden, document, and teach it.

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 认为，大多数人类写的软件既慢、漏洞多，又缺少明确规格。AI 会反复重写它们：证明、压测、加固、补文档。更大的判断是，这不只是更快地产生代码，而是软件工程真正开始成形。
original: 大多数人类软件很慢、漏洞多、规格不清且不正确。AI 会反复重写：形式化验证、压测、加固、写文档，并教会你它是怎么工作的。

rewrite: Rauch also shares a concrete security result: in 24 hours, Vercel's agent identified 6,817 vulnerabilities, including 580 critical or high severity, and patched 1,411 of them. The striking part is not the marketing number; it is the emerging loop where agents continuously inspect and repair software.
original: In just 24 hours: 6,817 vulnerabilities identified, 580 critical or high, and 1,411 already patched by Agent.

rewrite: Rauch 还给出了一个具体的安全结果：24 小时内，Vercel 的 agent 找出 6,817 个漏洞，其中 580 个属于 critical 或 high severity，并已经修复 1,411 个。真正值得注意的不是数字本身，而是 agent 持续检查、修复软件的闭环正在出现。
original: 24 小时内：发现 6,817 个漏洞，其中 580 个是 critical 或 high，已有 1,411 个被 Agent 修复。

rewrite: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan says GStack's /review skill is genuinely useful for preventing bugs. It is a small but telling example of where agent workflows become practical: not replacing review, but making review a routine, repeatable part of shipping.
original: GStack's /review skill is actually useful for preventing bugs still.

rewrite: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan 说，GStack 的 /review skill 确实能帮助预防 bug。这是 agent 工作流变得实用的一个小例子：不是取消 review，而是把 review 变成发布流程里稳定、可重复的一环。
original: GStack 的 /review skill 确实对预防 bug 有用。

sections.title: Agent 的新工作流 / Agents as Work Systems
sections.desc: 当 agent 代表项目持续运行，人类的角色开始从执行转向编排、审核和选择。

rewrite: Peter Steinberger asks whether individual usage limits still make sense as capabilities rise. His picture of the next workflow is an agent that represents a project, runs loops, and evolves the codebase, while humans mainly curate the automations. That is a shift from asking an assistant for output to supporting a long-lived project agent.
original: As capabilities increase you want to work with and support an agent that represents your project, that runs loops and evolves your codebase. The humans merely curate the automations.

rewrite: Peter Steinberger 追问：随着能力提升，按个人设置使用上限还合理吗？他想象的下一代工作流是，一个代表项目的 agent 自己跑循环、持续演进代码库，人类主要负责挑选和管理自动化。这意味着我们不再只是向助手要一次性输出，而是在维护一个长期运行的项目 agent。
original: 能力提升后，你会想和一个代表项目、运行循环并不断演进代码库的 agent 一起工作。人类只负责筛选自动化。

rewrite: Ryo Lu brings the human question back into an increasingly automated workflow: when we can make anything, do we still know what we want? He wants tools that help people form their own answers rather than skip that process, creating more room to think, care, and make together.
original: When we can make anything, do we still know what we want? I want tools that help us find our own answers, not skip the process of forming them. Not just more output, but more room to think, care, and make together.

rewrite: Ryo Lu 把问题拉回到自动化之外：当我们什么都能做时，还知道自己想要什么吗？他希望工具帮助人们形成自己的答案，而不是跳过这个过程，让大家有更多空间去思考、在乎，并一起创造。
original: 当我们什么都能做时，还知道自己想要什么吗？我想要的是帮助我们找到答案、而不是跳过形成答案过程的工具。不只是更多产出，而是更多一起思考、在乎和创造的空间。

sections.title: 从模型到组织 / Models Meet Organizations
sections.desc: 真正的 AI 落地不只在模型能力，也在于企业能否把 agent 接进真实的工作和约束。

rewrite: Replit CEO Amjad Masad says a Japanese financial institution completed in one week, with one person, a project that previously took six people six months. He frames the partnership as AI-powered software creation for enterprises facing labor shortages. The useful signal is operational: the promise is being measured in project duration and team size, not just model benchmarks.
original: SMFL recently in just one week, with one person, completed a project that previously required six people working for six months. Replit is partnering to bring AI-powered software creation to Japanese enterprises.

rewrite: Replit CEO Amjad Masad 说，一家日本金融机构最近用 1 个人、1 周完成了过去需要 6 个人做 6 个月的项目。他把这次合作放在日本企业面对劳动力短缺的背景下。这里的有效信号很具体：AI 的价值开始用项目周期和团队人数衡量，而不只是 benchmark。
original: SMFL 最近用 1 个人、1 周完成了过去需要 6 个人工作 6 个月的项目。Replit 将与其合作，把 AI 驱动的软件开发带给日本企业。

rewrite: Cat Wu announced that she is joining OpenAI to lead product management for Core Products. Her stated goal is to build agents that have your back and your team's, while keeping users in control and giving them more time for people and work they care about.
original: I'm joining OpenAI to lead product management for Core Products. Together, we'll build agents that have your back and your team's, and keep you in control, so you get more time for the people and work you love.

rewrite: Cat Wu 宣布加入 OpenAI，负责 Core Products 的产品管理。她给出的方向是构建能照顾你和团队的 agent，同时让用户保持控制，把时间还给真正重要的人和工作。
original: 我将加入 OpenAI，负责 Core Products 的产品管理。我们会一起构建照顾你和团队的 agent，并让你保持控制，从而拥有更多时间给重要的人和工作。

sections.title: 训练 agent 的代价 / The Cost of Training Agents
sections.desc: agent 的能力不是凭空出现的，训练环境、奖励信号和基础设施都必须更接近真实世界。

rewrite: Kevin Roose, after interviewing roughly 150 people connected to the labs building modern AI, says the future is neither predetermined nor safe by default. He argues for basic industry-wide testing before public deployment, comparing it to pharmaceutical safety testing, and for coordination that gives safety teams time to develop better controls. His historical point is equally important: many of the decisions that shaped AI happened in private, so recording how we got here matters.
original: I came away thinking both that there are some real risks ahead and some real needles that we'll need to thread as a society, but that we can do it. The choices that we make right now matter a lot.
We should require AI companies to test their models before offering them to the public.

rewrite: 采访过大约 150 位与现代 AI 实验室有关的人之后，Kevin Roose 认为，未来既不是命中注定，也不会自动安全。他主张在模型公开部署前建立类似药品的行业安全测试，并通过协调机制给安全团队留出开发控制手段的时间。他还提醒：塑造 AI 的很多决定发生在私下，所以记录我们是怎么走到这里的，本身就很重要。
original: 我最终认为，前方确实有真实风险，也有需要社会共同穿过的针眼，但我们做得到。现在做出的选择非常重要。我们应该要求 AI 公司在向公众提供模型前测试它们。

rewrite: Swyx highlights a result from Thinky Machines' Inkling: three times faster and five times cheaper while scoring the same on FrontierCode 2. He reads it as distillation without the usual tradeoff, and expects many more examples of this approach, especially for US-pretrained models. The practical implication is that useful capability may spread through efficient derivatives, not only larger frontier models.
original: 3x faster 5x cheaper but evals SAME ON FRONTIERCODE 2. This is distillation without tradeoffs. I think Thinky Machines' Inkling is one of the most underrated base models in the world.

rewrite: Swyx 关注了 Thinky Machines 的 Inkling：速度快 3 倍、成本低 5 倍，但在 FrontierCode 2 上的评测成绩相同。他把这看成几乎没有取舍的 distillation，并预计这种路线会越来越多，尤其是在美国预训练模型上。实际意义是：有用能力的扩散，可能更多来自高效的衍生模型，而不只是更大的 frontier model。
original: 快 3 倍、便宜 5 倍，但 FrontierCode 2 评测相同。这是没有取舍的 distillation。我认为 Thinky Machines 的 Inkling 是世界上最被低估的 base model 之一。
